title.rendered: Water supply interruption: Hebron and Itsoseng – 25 June 2026

content.rendered:
Residents in Madibeng Local Municipality who are supplied with water by the City of Tshwane (Hebron and Itsoseng) reservoir area are informed about a water supply interruption scheduled for 25 June 2026 from 08:00 to 16:00 (eight hours) to install bulk meters on the bulk supply network.

The affected areas will fall under Madibeng Local Municipality:

  • Hebron
  • Itsoseng

The contact persons (for internal enquiries only) are as follows:

  • Donald Ngonyama (Engineering Consultant): 079 622 9588
  • Lesego Lekubu (Project Manager): 082 940 6817
  • After hours: 012 358 2111/9999 or 080 1111 556

Residents are urged to make the following water-conservation measures part of their normal lifestyle:

  • Do not water or irrigate gardens with hosepipes or sprinkler systems between 06:00 and 18:00.
  • Do not wash vehicles with hosepipes.
  • Do not fill swimming pools.

Residents are urged to continue using grey water to water gardens and flush toilets. Where possible, water-saving devices should be installed.

Residents should report water leaks, burst pipes and all incidents where water is wasted.

Residents should make water conservation part of their everyday lives by making use of the following water-saving tips:

  • Install a low-flow shower head and tap aerators where possible.
  • Use a dual-flush toilet cistern.
  • Plant indigenous or drought-resistant shrubs in the garden.
  • Use a broom instead of a hosepipe when cleaning driveways or patios.
  • Collect rainwater to reuse in the garden or wash the car.
  • Cover the swimming pool to reduce water evaporation.
  • Take a short shower rather than a bath.
  • Close a running tap while brushing teeth or shaving.
  • Regularly check toilets and taps for leaks.

title.rendered: City of Tshwane water systems show steady recovery following Rand Water maintenance – 1 June 2026

content.rendered:
The City of Tshwane is pleased to report continued progress in the recovery of its water distribution network following the completion of Rand Water’s planned maintenance programme. Most of the City’s reservoirs, towers and supply systems have remained stable throughout the recovery period, with water supply being maintained across most affected areas.

According to Rand Water, the Palmiet System is currently pumping at 89% capacity as it continues to stabilise. Despite the system not yet operating at full capacity, the ongoing improvement in storage levels across Tshwane is a positive indication that the network is steadily returning to normal operating conditions.

Region 1 continues to receive focused operational attention as recovery efforts advance. Reservoirs supplying Mabopane, Soshanguve L, Kruisfontein and portions of the Rosslyn/Magaliesberg System remain at lower-than-desired levels, largely due to the complexity and sensitivity of these networks. While some residents may continue to experience reduced water pressure, particularly in higher-lying areas and tower-fed zones, water continues to be distributed through the system as storage levels gradually improve. Targeted operational interventions remain in place to strengthen recovery and support affected communities.

 

The Region 3 network remains stable and continues to perform well overall. Most reservoirs are operating at healthy levels and are providing reliable supply to consumers. Although portions of the Magalies, Findlay West and Atteridgeville Low Level Systems are recovering at a slower pace, these areas continue to receive water while storage levels rebuild. Residents across most of Region 3 can expect normal water supply, with only isolated pressure fluctuations possible in some elevated areas during peak consumption periods.

Region 4 also remains stable, with the majority of the network functioning effectively. While reservoirs within the Rooihuiskraal and Pretoriusrand Systems are still recovering and remain under close monitoring, water supply continues to be maintained. Consumers supplied from these systems may occasionally experience lower pressure during periods of high demand, however, the overall network remains resilient and continues to recover steadily.

The City acknowledges the cooperation and patience demonstrated by residents throughout this recovery period. Following a major bulk water maintenance programme, reservoirs and towers require time to refill and stabilise before the system can fully normalise. Encouragingly, all affected systems are showing signs of improvement and recovery efforts continue to yield positive results across the network.

The City remains committed to closely monitoring system performance and implementing operational interventions wherever necessary to accelerate recovery.

Residents are encouraged to continue using water responsibly, as this will assist in restoring storage levels more rapidly and strengthening the resilience of the network.

 

Further updates will be provided as recovery progresses.

title.rendered: Rand Water to embark on phased maintenance work at its Palmiet, Zuikerbosch and Mapleton Systems which supply water to parts of Tshwane- 24 May 2026

content.rendered:
Rand Water will carry out two-phased annual maintenance of its infrastructure at the Palmiet, Zuikerbosch and Mapleton Systems to improve its network’s reliability and efficiency ahead of the start of the winter season. The first phase of this essential work will take place from Friday, 29 May 2026, to Tuesday, 2 June 2026.

The planned maintenance work, according to the water utility, will coincide with Eskom’s planned critical maintenance activities which will enhance operational flexibility across key Rand Water systems to reduce the risk of plant trips and equipment failures.

title.rendered: The City of Tshwane’s Regions 1, 3 and 4 water network system update – 12 February 2026

content.rendered:
Some of the City of Tshwane’s reservoirs in Regions 1, 3 and 4, which have been struggling to recover from their depletion since last week following inflow challenges, have shown some signs of stability, their low-level status notwithstanding.

The Ga-Rankuwa and Mabopane Central reservoirs are stable and operating normally. The Pretoriusrand Reservoir has recovered and is also at stable levels.

In the high-consumption areas, the Atteridgeville HL and Laudium reservoirs are stable, however, consumption remains significantly high and continues to place strain on the system.

The systems that are still experiencing major challenges include the Mabopane Main and Kruisfontein reservoirs, which are still at critically low levels.

The Mabopane, Soshanguve L and Soshanguve DD reservoirs are still empty. Consequently, there is no active supply in these systems at this stage and the City’s technical teams are facing difficulties in restoring flows due to the network’s depletion.

Customers are urged to use water sparingly to support the City’s recovery efforts.

The City will continue to monitor the situation closely and provide further updates as conditions change.

title.rendered: Tshwane’s water network system continues to be under severe strain- 11 February 2026

content.rendered:
The City of Tshwane’s water distribution network is still under severe strain as the inflow from Rand Water persists at a low level, which has been exacerbated by high consumption.

The exceedingly high consumption by consumers has adversely impacted the main receiving reservoirs in Regions 1, 3 and 4, which are at critical levels, with some already running empty.

As of this morning, Wednesday, 11 February 2026, the Soshanguve Block L and Mabopane Reservoirs were still empty.  Our teams are closely monitoring these two reservoirs, which continue to experience the most strain and require sustained inflows before meaningful recovery can be reflected.

Pretoriusrand, Klipgat, Kruisfontein and Mabopane main reservoirs still reflect critically low levels, while the Soshanguve Block DD Reservoir is stable, albeit at critically low levels.

The Laudium and Atteridgeville HL Reservoirs, which were depleting at an accelerated pace yesterday afternoon, 10 February 2026, have now been stabilised. These systems are currently performing within acceptable levels.

It must be emphasised that the persistent high consumption levels are negatively impacting the recovery process of the affected reservoirs. We are once again imploring customers to reduce their consumption levels to save the City’s distribution network from collapsing.

The City will continue to monitor the situation closely and provide further updates as conditions change.

title.rendered: Palmiet water supply system shows gradual but uneven recovery following Rand Water maintenance  -18 December 2025

content.rendered:
Following the successful completion of Rand Water’s scheduled maintenance programme, the City of Tshwane confirms that recovery on the Palmiet supply system is underway. Water is steadily re-entering the network; however, the scale and complexity of the system mean that pressure restoration and reservoir replenishment are occurring progressively rather than simultaneously across all supply zones.

The Palmiet system is showing pockets of improvement, although the overall recovery remains uneven and, in some areas, unstable. While water is moving through the network, it will take time for adequate pressure to build up to fully recharge all reservoirs, particularly those serving high-lying communities that depend on sustained system strength.

Encouraging progress has been recorded in several parts of the network. The Louwlardia and The Reeds supply zones continue to demonstrate sustained improvement, alongside all areas that are supplied by the Soshanguve DD Reservoirs and the Atteridgeville Low-level (LL) Reservoir, where pressure and supply are gradually stabilising as the system strengthens.

Despite these positive developments, notable challenges persist in certain areas. Communities supplied by the Kruisfontein Reservoir, Soshanguve L Reservoir, Laudium Reservoir, Atteridgeville High-level (HL) Reservoir, Lotus Gardens Reservoir, as well as Kosmosdal Reservoir and Sunderland Ridge Reservoir, continue to experience low pressure and slow recovery, which is largely due to elevation constraints and the time required for the broader network to fully recharge.

As a responsive municipality, the City of Tshwane has activated alternative water supply interventions, including the deployment of water tankers and bowsers to affected areas. These measures are intended to alleviate hardship while the Palmiet system continues its recovery, and they are being coordinated on the ground to prioritise the most affected communities.

The City continues to closely monitor reservoir levels and overall system behaviour, with the expectation that further recovery and pressure build-up will occur over the coming days as the Palmiet system gradually stabilises and regains operational balance.

The City of Tshwane apologises for the inconvenience experienced and thanks residents for their patience, cooperation and understanding as work continues to restore the water supply network to full and sustainable operation.

title.rendered: Temporary water supply interruption due to planned Mabopane Main Reservoir recovery maintenance   8 August 2025

content.rendered:
The City of Tshwane is appealing to all residents in Mabopane and surrounding areas for patience and understanding as it undertakes an emergency maintenance intervention at Mabopane Main Reservoir.

This critical intervention will commence on Tuesday, 12 August 2025, and is expected to last for approximately 24 hours, concluding in the evening of Wednesday, 13 August 2025.

Mabopane Main Reservoir is currently under severe pressure due to extremely high water consumption. Despite sufficient bulk supply, the system is unable to raise reservoir levels beyond 30%, making it impossible to maintain stable pressure and flow to the community.

In an effort to stabilise the system, the reservoir outlet will be temporarily closed to allow for recovery. This action is necessary to restore capacity and ensure sustainable and reliable water supply moving forward.

The intervention will benefit areas supplied by the following critical reservoirs:

  • Mabopane Central
  • Mabopane Main
  • Mabopane Reservoir
  • Higher-lying zones in Mabopane Block B

These areas have been experiencing intermittent water supply since the recent Rand Water shutdown and this recovery initiative is intended to bring relief and long-term improvement.

The City pleads for the community’s cooperation and understanding during this period. Once the reservoir has reached acceptable levels, normal water supply will resume.

The City of Tshwane remains committed to ensuring stable and improved water provision to all residents and thanks the community for their continued support during this critical intervention.

title.rendered: Temporary shutdown of Themba Water Treatment Plant leads to an interruption in the supply zone – 27 June 2025

content.rendered:
The City of Tshwane regrets to inform customers residing in Themba and surrounding areas about a temporary water supply interruption following the shutdown of Themba Water Treatment Plant. This decision was taken as a necessary precaution to protect public health due to water quality challenges currently experienced at the plant.

The challenges stem from a sewer discharge that has been detected flowing into the Apies River, which feeds into the Leeukraal Dam – the primary water source for Themba Water Treatment Plant. As a result, the raw water quality has deteriorated, making it unsafe for processing and distribution in its current state.

While the City initially reduced the plant’s pumping capacity to manage the issue, the situation has unfortunately reached a point where continuing to pump is unsustainable. In an effort to prevent poor-quality water from reaching residents, operations at the plant have been temporarily halted until the water quality stabilises.

To assist communities during this period, roaming water tankers will be dispatched to the affected areas to ensure continued access to clean water. These tankers will be strategically routed to reach as many residents as possible until normal supply can be restored.

The following areas are currently affected:

  • Dilopye
  • Hammanskraal West
  • Lepheng
  • Majaneng
  • Refentse
  • Renstown
  • Sekampaneng
  • Suurman
  • Unit 7

The City understands the inconvenience this causes and is working diligently to resolve the situation.

Residents are kindly urged to use water sparingly. Your cooperation is vital as we work to restore safe and reliable water supply to all affected communities.

Further updates will be communicated as new information becomes available

Motorists are notified of a temporary closure of the N4 Highway between the Simon Vermooten and Solomon Mahlangu interchanges, east of Tshwane, on Sunday, 15 June 2025, to allow for critical infrastructure work.   • Affected route: N4 Highway in both directions between the Simon Vermooten and Solomon Mahlangu interchanges

In summary, the planned construction will entail the following aspects:

  • High-voltage conductors will be strung across the N4 Highway using tension equipment.
  • Conductors will maintain a minimum clearance height of 23 m above the roadway, in full compliance with safety standards.
  • Transmission masts have been pre-approved and are located outside the road reserve.
  • Detour routes and temporary signage will be clearly marked.
  • TMPD officers will be on-site to manage and direct traffic.

The City of Tshwane apologises for any inconvenience caused and appreciates the public’s understanding as we work to enhance the city’s energy infrastructure.

title.rendered: Themba Water Treatment Plant temporarily shut down  29 May 2025

content.rendered:
The City of Tshwane wishes to inform residents and stakeholders of the temporary shutdown of Themba Water Treatment Plant today, 29 May 2025, due to a critical failure in the communication cables that connect the chlorine dosing system, actuators and vacuum regulators.

This system, which is housed inside the plant, doses chlorine during the water treatment process. A treatment plant cannot run without chlorine, and the City was therefore compelled to temporarily shut down operations.

Earlier today, a contractor was on-site to repair the vacuum regulator on the chlorine dosing equipment. The component was removed and taken to a workshop for further repairs. Upon attempting to restart the dosing system and the plant, a significant valve leak was discovered, which now necessitates replacement.

Unfortunately, the required valve is not currently in stock. The contractor will begin sourcing the part on Friday, 30 May 2025. In the meantime, fault-finding and rewiring of the communication system will also begin on the same day.

The team has finally managed to connect the cable end box to the main transformer following a lengthy and gruelling installation process. The testing team has now successfully completed 95% of the required tests before the switching team can energise the substation.

The only remaining test the team is currently working on is the communication between Zwartkop Substation and Kwagga Infeed Substation. The two substations must be linked to ensure the protection of the Zwartkop transformer. The high-voltage circuit breaker that protects the Zwartkop main transformer in case there is a fault on the supply line is located at Kwagga Infeed Substation.

Once the linking process is finalised, the switching team will energise the substation and the restoration of the power supply to the affected consumers will be done gradually to avoid a system overload.

title.rendered: WATER SUPPLY INTERRUPTION: HIGHVELD EXT 65 – 12 November 2024

content.rendered:
Scheduled upgrades to the water supply network are being undertaken in Highveld Ext 65 on Kaoline Street and Olievenhoutbosch Road.

Although interruptions to the water supply are avoided at all costs, it may be interrupted from time to time on Tuesday, 12 November 2024, from 08:00 to 18:00 for a water connection into the bulk water pipeline.

The following areas will be affected:

  • Highveld Ext 2, 7 and 8
  • Irene Ext 52, 147, 155, 156, 157 and 185

The following notable places will be affected within the affected areas:

  • Centurion Academy
  • Centurion Residential Estate & Country Club
  • Hyundai Centurion
  • Makro Centurion
  • Southdowns Centre

The contact persons (for internal enquiries only) are as follows:

  • Cleopas Kgobe (Engineering Consultant): 012 358 1527
  • Dlozi Matjeni (System Inspector): 012 358 6817
  • After hours: 012 358 2111/9999 or 080 1111 556

Residents are urged to make the following water-conservation measures part of their normal lifestyle:

  • Do not water or irrigate gardens with hosepipes or sprinkler systems between 06:00 and 18:00.
  • Do not wash vehicles with hosepipes.
  • Do not fill swimming pools.

Residents are urged to keep on using grey water to water gardens and flush toilets. Residents should report water leaks, burst pipes and all incidents where water is wasted. Where possible, water-saving devices should be installed.

Residents should make water conservation part of their everyday lives by making use of the following water-saving tips:

  • Install a low-flow shower head and tap aerators where possible.
  • Use a dual-flush toilet cistern.
  • Plant indigenous or drought-resistant shrubs in the garden.
  • Use a broom instead of a hosepipe when cleaning driveways or patios.
  • Collect rainwater to reuse in the garden or wash the car.
  • Cover the swimming pool to reduce water evaporation.
  • Take a shower rather than a bath.
  • Close a running tap while brushing teeth or shaving.
  • Regularly check toilets and taps for leaks.

Residents can use the following numbers to report water-related incidents:

Incident Telephone number
No water supply, burst water pipes, leaking meters or blocked street sewers 012 358 9999 or

080 1111 556
Illegal water connections 012 358 9060
Non-payment 012 345 8514
Account enquiries 012 358 9999

 

Regards
